## The diff

The change is UNCOMMITTED working-tree changes against HEAD (7d10b8e5).

Get the tracked-file diff with:
  git diff HEAD

Four files are NEW and untracked, so they will NOT appear in that diff. Read them in full with the Read tool:
  - CONTEXT.md
  - src/components/global/cta-slide-in.astro
  - src/components/global/cta-sticky-bar.astro
  - src/utils/cta-analytics.ts

Ignore `.claude/settings.local.json` (unrelated, pre-existing).

## The spec

The spec has TWO parts, and the second SUPERSEDES the first wherever they conflict.

### Part 1 — the original handoff document
Read `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro/temp/quiz-attention-surface-handoff.md` in full.

### Part 2 — the settled decisions (these OVERRIDE the handoff)
These came out of a requirements interview with the repo owner and are binding:

1. Two surfaces: sticky bar and slide-in. NO lightbox / blocking popup. The existing `modal-popup.astro` is DELETED entirely, along with its CSS.
2. Slide-in goes on BOTH blog posts AND glossary entries (the handoff said blog only).
3. "One pinned surface per page" governs PINNED (fixed-position) surfaces only. The in-flow `cta-banner.astro` and `link-sidebar.astro` are unaffected and may coexist with either.
4. NO surface asks for an email. All link to the quiz cover. Email capture stays where it is, in the quiz's own end-of-quiz capture step.
5. PREFILL IS SHELVED. The slide-in must NOT carry any answer into the quiz. It poses a rhetorical question with TWO buttons that both go to the same quiz URL, differing only by `utm_content`, so the numbers say which framing pulled.
6. The handoff's "Quiz funnel spec" section (5-7 questions, capture email at Q3-Q4, gate results behind opt-in) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. The quiz must not be touched.
7. Sticky bar: bottom edge, full width, one line + one button. DISMISSABLE, suppressed for the rest of the SESSION only. Pure overlay (does NOT reserve space / no body padding) — the owner wants to see how it looks first.
8. Slide-in: trigger at 50% SCROLL (not a time delay). Dismissable via the X ONLY (not click-outside, not swipe). Suppressed 15 days in localStorage. The suppression clock starts when it APPEARS, not when dismissed. It must use a NEW storage key, not inherit the modal's old key.
9. Slide-in on mobile: shown, full width.
10. Sticky bar page set. ON: home, blog index, blog/all, blog category pages, glossary index, and content pages (those behind `src/pages/[id].astro`) BY DEFAULT. OFF for content pages that are `noIndex` in frontmatter, plus `privacy-policy` and `contact-us` by name. OFF entirely for: course pages, quiz pages, 404, sitemap, about-this-site, newsletter-subscribe, newsletter-signup-thanks, loopy-scratch, ai-failure-modes, and blog posts / glossary entries (those get the slide-in).
11. PostHog is the only analytics layer. Events `cta_shown` and `cta_dismissed`, fired for BOTH surfaces (including the sticky bar). Clicks stay on autocapture.
12. Both new surfaces keep A/B variant support (`CTA_VARIANT` / `AB_TEST_ENABLED`), which stays `null`/`false` at launch.
13. All copy lives in `src/constants/cta.ts`. No copy props on the components.
14. NO automated tests and NO ADR — both explicitly declined by the owner.

## Your brief

Report:
(a) requirements the spec asked for that are MISSING or PARTIAL;
(b) behaviour in the diff that WASN'T ASKED FOR (scope creep);
(c) requirements that look implemented but where the IMPLEMENTATION LOOKS WRONG.

Quote the spec line (by number for Part 2, or by quoted text for Part 1) for each finding.

Verify claims against the actual code rather than trusting comments. In particular, actually trace: the scroll-trigger arithmetic; the suppression key names and which storage each uses; whether the clock starts on show or dismiss; whether both buttons really point at the same URL with different utm_content; and which routes import which component (check every route file listed in item 10).

Under 400 words. Be specific and quote code.

1	# Handoff: Quiz Attention Surfaces (Sticky Bars + Slide-ins)
2	
3	**Purpose:** Start implementing sticky bars and slide-in popups on the APR site to drive people into a quiz funnel.
4	
5	**Date:** 2026-08-06
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	We researched the current state of popups, sliders, and other attention surfaces, focused specifically on getting people to *start* (and finish) a quiz. Decisions below are settled; this doc is the spec to build against.
10	
11	Full research + sources: `~/Documents/Obsidian/MarkPKM/OutsideContent/Generated/Popup and Quiz Funnel Research - What Works.md` (in Mark's vault, not this repo). Read it for benchmark numbers and cited sources. This handoff carries only the implementation-relevant conclusions.
12	
13	## Core decisions
14	
15	- **Two surfaces in scope:** a **sticky bar** and a **slide-in**. No lightbox/full-screen popups (mobile SEO penalty + brand tone).
16	- **One surface per page.** A page shows a sticky bar OR a slide-in, never both. Never stack two fixed elements at the same edge.
17	- **Surface-to-page mapping:**
18	  - Sticky bar: site-wide persistent invite (home, course pages, general).
19	  - Slide-in: blog/article posts only, since those readers are engaged.
20	- **Brand-styled:** both must use APR site fonts/colors so they read as first-party, not a third-party ad.
21	
22	## Sticky bar spec
23	
24	- Horizontal, full-width, pinned to an edge.
25	- **Mobile: bottom** (thumb zone, avoids top browser chrome, SEO-safe). Use top only for pure announcements / urgency countdowns.
26	- One line of copy + one tappable button.
27	- Do not stack with cookie banner, chat bubble, or other fixed bottom elements.
28	- Variables to test: placement (top/bottom), copy, color/contrast. (No timing variable exists for a sticky bar.)
29	
30	## Slide-in spec
31	
32	- Position: bottom-left or bottom-right, under ~1/6 of screen.
33	- Trigger: time delay or scroll (~50% scroll is the default to build against).
34	- **Frequency capping:** show once per visitor, suppress for X days (cookie). Never re-fire every pageload.
35	- **Dismissal:** clear X; click-outside / swipe-away on mobile; stays dismissed for the session.
36	- **Non-blocking:** never darken or lock the page (this is what keeps it from being a lightbox).
37	- Animation: enters from its own edge, ~0.3s, not bouncy.
38	- Content: headline + one line + one button, or single email field.
39	- **Two-step / micro-commitment:** put the quiz's first question (or a yes/no) directly in the slide-in, e.g. "What Type of ScrumMaster Are You? [Start]".
40	- Mobile: it will take more space than on desktop; accept or shrink. Never alongside a bottom sticky bar.
41	
42	Reference designs (quiz-in-a-slide-in): **Salt Strong** (reported +185%), **Spruce / CBD** ("Need help choosing?").
43	
44	## Quiz funnel spec (the destination)
45	
46	- Outcome-driven "What/Which" title; state time cost upfront ("2 minutes").
47	- Cover page mobile-optimized: title, description, button stacked above the featured image.
48	- 5 to 7 questions (completion drops sharply after 8).
49	- Capture email mid-quiz (Q3 to Q4), reveal results only after opt-in.
50	
51	## Measurement / analytics to build in
52	
53	The honest measure across both surfaces is the chain: **click -> quiz start -> completion -> opt-in.** Tag each entry point (sticky bar vs slide-in) so we know which produces *finishers*, not just clickers.
54	
55	- **Slide-in:** impressions, CTR (clicks / impressions), dismiss rate, device (mobile/desktop), source page, scroll depth / time-on-page before click, first-time vs returning.
56	- **Sticky bar (simpler):** CTR (clicks / pageviews shown), device split, source page. Skip impression tracking (= pageviews), dismiss rate, and timing diagnostics.
57	- **Skip for now (both):** heatmaps, session recordings, multi-touch attribution.
58	
59	Note APR analytics architecture before wiring events: raw data lives in this Astro repo, analysis/experiments live in the vault. Check existing analytics setup here before adding a new tracking mechanism.
60	
61	## Open questions for implementation
62	
63	- What quiz engine/tool are we using (self-built vs Interact/similar)? Affects opt-in placement and analytics hooks.
64	- Which analytics layer captures the events (existing GA/GSC setup vs custom)?
65	- Cookie/consent handling for frequency capping (must respect the site's existing consent approach).
66	
67	## Suggested skills for the implementing session
68	
69	- **prototype** — sanity-check the slide-in state model (trigger -> show -> dismiss -> cap) and the sticky-bar responsive behavior before committing to the real components.
70	- **codebase-design** — decide the seam: one shared "attention surface" module vs two separate components, and where the trigger/capping logic lives.
71	- **tdd** — build the frequency-capping / trigger logic test-first (it's the fiddly, easy-to-get-wrong part).
72	- **code-review** — review the change against APR repo standards before merge.
73

1	/**
2	 * PostHog events for the pinned CTA surfaces.
3	 *
4	 * Clicks are left to PostHog's autocapture, which already picks up the
5	 * `data-ph-capture-attribute-*` attributes on the links. Only the two things
6	 * autocapture cannot see are captured explicitly: that a surface appeared, and
7	 * that someone closed it.
8	 *
9	 * `cta_shown` fires for the sticky bar too, even though its impressions are
10	 * nearly pageviews. "Nearly" is the problem: the bar is withheld from noIndex
11	 * pages, from two named slugs, and from anyone who dismissed it earlier in the
12	 * session, so reconstructing impressions from pageviews after the fact would
13	 * mean replaying all three rules against history. One event now is cheaper.
14	 *
15	 * The chain these close is: cta_shown -> (autocaptured click) -> quiz_started
16	 * -> the quiz's own capture step.
17	 */
18	
19	import type { Attribution } from '@/constants/cta';
20	
21	export type CtaSurface = 'sticky-bar' | 'slide-in';
22	
23	type CtaEvent = 'cta_shown' | 'cta_dismissed';
24	
25	/**
26	 * PostHog is loaded as the inline snippet in posthog.astro, not as an npm
27	 * package, so it is reachable only as a global and only once that snippet has
28	 * run. Typed narrowly here rather than augmenting Window globally: this is the
29	 * only client code that needs it.
30	 */
31	type PostHogGlobal = {
32	  capture: (event: string, properties?: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
33	};
34	
35	/**
36	 * Send a CTA surface event. Silently does nothing if PostHog has not loaded,
37	 * because an ad blocker or a slow network must never break the surface itself.
38	 */
39	export function captureCtaEvent(
40	  event: CtaEvent,
41	  surface: CtaSurface,
42	  attribution: Attribution
43	): void {
44	  const posthog = (window as unknown as { posthog?: PostHogGlobal }).posthog;
45	  if (!posthog) return;
46	
47	  posthog.capture(event, {
48	    surface,
49	    attribution,
50	    path: window.location.pathname,
51	  });
52	}
53

content.text:
## (a) Missing / partial

**1. Slide-in can never fire if the page is already past halfway on load.** `cta-slide-in.astro:206-220` arms only a `scroll` listener; there is no check at init. An anchor deep-link (`/blog/x/#some-heading`), a back-navigation with scroll restoration, or a short article where the reader lands past 50% fires no `scroll` event, so `reveal()` never runs. Spec item 8: "trigger at 50% SCROLL". The arithmetic itself (`window.scrollY / (documentElement.scrollHeight - innerHeight) >= 0.5`, with the `scrollable <= 0` guard) is correct.

**2. Copy is placeholder, not shipped copy.** `cta.ts:81` — "FIRST DRAFT: the four sticky-bar/slide-in strings are AI-drafted placeholders awaiting Mark's rewrite." Item 13 puts all copy in `cta.ts`; that part holds, but the surfaces would launch with unreviewed text. One string escapes `cta.ts` entirely: `aria-label="Quiz invitation"` hardcoded at `cta-slide-in.astro:72`.

## (b) Not asked for

**3. `CONTEXT.md`** is a brand-new top-level doc plus a `CLAUDE.md` section describing it. Nothing in either spec part asks for a project glossary, and item 14 declines the one documentation artifact that *was* discussed ("NO automated tests and NO ADR").

**4. Dead code left behind:** `clearCtaSuppression()` (`storage.ts:157`) has no caller, and `UTMMedium` (`tracking.ts:12`) still carries `'popup'` after `modal-popup.astro` was deleted — the one thing that emitted it.

## (c) Implemented but wrong

**5. Dismissing the slide-in leaves a visible strip on desktop.** `dismiss()` (`cta-slide-in.astro:184-187`) only re-adds `translate-y-full`; it never re-adds `hidden`. The panel is `sm:bottom-6`, so `translateY(100%)` moves its top edge to 24px *above* the viewport bottom — a 24px band of white card, 2px blue border, and the top of the `absolute top-2 right-2` close button stays on screen and clickable, forever. It also stays in the a11y tree and tab order. Item 8 says the X is the dismissal; this doesn't dismiss it. Adding `hidden` after the 300ms transition fixes it.

## Verified correct

Both buttons → `CTA_PRIMARY.buttonLink` differing only by `utm_content=not-sure` / `i-think-i-know` (item 5). New keys `agilePainRelief:ctaSlideInLastShown` (localStorage, 15d) and `agilePainRelief:ctaStickyBarDismissed` (sessionStorage), neither inheriting `agilePainRelief:modalLastShown` (items 7, 8). Clock starts in `reveal()`, not `dismiss()` (item 8). Route set exactly matches item 10 — only the 8 listed files import either component; no page imports both; `showStickyBar` excludes `noIndex` + `privacy-policy` + `contact-us`. No body padding (item 7). `astro check`: 0 errors.
